title: Atomic helpers
description:
Write four functions that update a qword in memory atomically (as they would need to be with several threads, although the tests use one):

| Function | Effect | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `fetch_add(address, n)` | adds n to the qword | the value **before** the add (use `lock xadd`) |
| `swap_in(address, value)` | stores value | the old value (use `xchg`) |
| `cas(address, expected, desired)` | stores desired only if the qword equals expected | 1 if it stored, 0 if not (use `lock cmpxchg`) |
| `atomic_max(address, value)` | stores value if it is larger than the qword, with a compare-and-swap loop | the value before |

starter.solution.asm:
fetch_add:
        mov     rax, [rdi]
        add     [rdi], rsi
        ret

swap_in:
        mov     rax, [rdi]
        mov     [rdi], rsi
        ret

cas:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

atomic_max:
        mov     rax, [rdi]
        ret

solution.solution.asm:
fetch_add:
        mov     rax, rsi
        lock xadd [rdi], rax
        ret

swap_in:
        mov     rax, rsi
        xchg    [rdi], rax
        ret

cas:
        mov     rax, rsi
        lock cmpxchg [rdi], rdx
        sete    al
        movzx   eax, al
        ret

atomic_max:
        mov     rax, [rdi]
.retry: cmp     rax, rsi
        jge     .done
        lock cmpxchg [rdi], rsi
        jne     .retry
.done:  ret

hints: `lock xadd [rdi], rax` adds `rax` to memory and leaves the old memory value in `rax`, exactly the return value wanted. `xchg` with memory is atomic by itself.
`cmpxchg` compares memory with `rax`, so put `expected` in `rax` first. Afterwards ZF says whether it stored: `sete al` turns that into 1 or 0.
rules: Use lock cmpxchg for the compare-and-swap.
Use xchg with memory in swap_in.
unitTests:
test "fetch and add"
    fetch_add(@[5], 3) == 5
    fetch_add(@[5], 3) => [8]
    fetch_add(@[10], -10) => [0]
test "swap"
    swap_in(@[7], 9) == 7
    swap_in(@[7], 9) => [9]
test "compare and swap"
    cas(@[5], 5, 9) == 1
    cas(@[5], 5, 9) => [9]
    cas(@[5], 4, 9) == 0
    cas(@[5], 4, 9) => [5]
test "atomic max"
    atomic_max(@[40], 75) == 40
    atomic_max(@[40], 75) => [75]
    atomic_max(@[40], 10) => [40]
    atomic_max(@[-5], -1) => [-1]
